papers.title: The use of inorganic process control agents to mill titanium‑niobium powders suitable for the selective laser melting process
papers.abstract: Alloying titanium (Ti) with niobium (Nb) offers the ability to develop a low-stiffness Ti alloy. The established methodologies for the fabrication of powders suitable for SLM processes are based on atomisation processes, which require high volume powder production to be financially viable. Consequently, these are unsuited for small batches used in bespoke alloys (e.g., Ti-Nb alloys). This work highlights the potential for milled powders as a cheaper feedstock for the SLM process. When following the established practice of using organic PCAs, this leads to the creation of interstitial phases during SLM fabrication. To alleviate that, this study puts forward the use of inorganic PCAs, such as tin (Sn) and calcium (Ca), to produce SLM-suitable powder. The use of inorganic PCAs, especially Ca, is effective, rendering the resultant powder with physical properties appropriate for the SLM process. These inorganic PCAs allow the fabrication of homogeneous Ti-Nb alloys with suitable hardness.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发低成本SLM用Ti-Nb合金粉末。
summary_zh.method: 使用无机过程控制剂研磨粉末，避免有机PCA引入的间隙相。

summary_en.motivation: To develop a cost-effective method for producing Ti-Nb alloy powders suitable for selective laser melting, enabling small-batch bespoke alloys without the high volume requirements of atomization.
summary_en.method: Inorganic process control agents (tin and calcium) were used during ball milling of elemental Ti and Nb powders to prevent interstitial phase contamination during SLM.
summary_en.result: Calcium was effective as a PCA, yielding powders with appropriate flowability and particle size, and SLM-fabricated parts showed homogeneous microstructure and adequate hardness.
summary_en.validation: Powder properties (morphology, size, flow) and SLM part hardness were characterized using SEM, XRD, and microhardness testing.
